subject: Customer security notification: anomalous token use and request for artifact transfer
messages:
From: Lisa Thompson <lisa.thompson@northbridge.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 18:03:00 -0700
Subject: Suspicious token activity detected — logs attached

Hi Karthik,

We observed several anomalous API calls from a set of tokens tied to one of our test integrations on 2027-06-11 between 01:40–02:10 UTC. The patterns look like automated replay attempts (high request rate, short intervals). I've attached a CSV with the raw access rows we pulled from our proxy (nb_incident_log_20270611.csv).

We need two things from Redwood to help us triage:
- A brief confirmation of whether those token IDs are still active on your side and any metadata you can share (creation time, last use).
- A copy of the access snapshot or audit extract that shows the same token usages from Redwood's logs for cross-correlation.

This is on our critical path for tomorrow's regulatory meeting; could you confirm receipt and an ETA for artifacts? If you prefer a secure upload channel for any PII we can provide an S3 presigned link.

Thanks — appreciate the quick turnaround.

— Lisa Thompson
Senior Ops Lead, Platform Security
Northbridge Financial
attachments: nb_incident_log_20270611.csv
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Lisa Thompson <lisa.thompson@northbridge.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 19:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Suspicious token activity detected — logs attached

Hi Lisa — thanks for the heads up and for sending the CSV. We received your file and have started an initial correlation run.

Ack + preliminary plan (high level):
1) We will produce a timebound audit extract for the token IDs you included (delivery: encrypted PDF + CSV).
2) We will confirm token lifecycle state (active / deleted / rotated) and associated client_id info.
3) If cross-correlation shows unexpected Redwood-side usage, we'll escalate to incident response and share forensics artifacts (PCAPs, request traces) via your preferred secure channel.

Requests from our side to speed triage:
- Can you confirm the token IDs (redacted if necessary) and the exact 15-minute windows you care about?
- Please provide the S3 presigned URL or a preferred secure upload method (we can also accept an encrypted ZIP via the Drive folder link).
- Are there any regulatory constraints (data masking for cardholder data, PII redaction) we should apply before sharing logs?

CC'ing Marissa (Customer Success) to help coordinate timeline and Neha (Security Ops) to own the audit extract generation. Our target is to get the initial extract to you within 6 hours of finalizing the token list and access window.

I'll follow up with the extraction ticket and a short M.A.P. (mutual action plan) that lists owners and expected delivery times.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Security & Trust Manager
Redwood Inference
attachments: prelim_ack.txt
From: Lisa Thompson <lisa.thompson@northbridge.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: ops@northbridge.com
Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2027 02:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Suspicious token activity detected — logs attached

Thanks Karthik — forwarding the exact token IDs and the 01:38–02:04 UTC window (attached). We spun up an S3 presigned link for you: https://s3.amazonaws.com/northbridge-incident/nb-share-20270611?X-Amz-Expires=3600 (expires in 1 hour).

Notes:
- The CSV includes internal user_id hashes; we can't share raw PII but can provide hashed identifiers.
- Regulatory constraint: please ensure any shared extracts strip full card numbers and replace with last-4 per our compliance checklist.

I'll leave this with your security ops team — Marissa, Neha, thanks for coordinating. I've also attached a short doc with our initial internal summary: investigation_summary.docx

— Lisa
attachments: investigation_summary.docx

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Lisa Thompson <lisa.thompson@northbridge.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2027 11:24:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Suspicious token activity detected — logs attached

Lisa / Northbridge team — thanks for the token list and the S3 link. We pulled the window you specified and produced the following deliverables:

Deliverables (attached / links):
- redwood_access_snapshot.pdf — timebound audit extract (matches your 01:38–02:04 UTC window).
- nb_cross_correlation.csv — combined rows where timestamps and request IDs matched within +/-2s.
- forensic_notes.txt — short runbook of initial findings and recommended containment steps.

Key findings (summary):
- The token IDs you provided show activity originating from two distinct IP blocks; one block corresponds to your test harness, the other is an unknown external egress.
- Token status: both tokens were active at the time of the events; one token was rotated by your team at 03:15 UTC per your summary doc.
- No evidence of exfiltration of cardholder PANs in Redwood logs; we did see multiple failed parameter combinations that aligned with automated fuzzing.

Next steps / owners:
- Neha to open an internal IR ticket if cross-correlation indicates Redwood-side compromise (Neha -> will confirm within 2 hours).
- Marissa to coordinate a joint postmortem timeline and customer-facing summary (Marissa -> draft by EOD).
- Karthik to prepare the compliance-ready artifact bundle (logs with required redactions) and share via the Drive folder link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-northbridge-exchange

A couple of asks for Northbridge to close the loop:
- Please confirm whether you want us to redact the hashed user IDs further or keep them as-is for correlation.
- Confirm whether you want a joint postmortem (co-authored) or a customer-only summary.

I'll attach the artifact bundle to the Drive folder and send you the final encrypted ZIP. Thanks again for quick coordination.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Security & Trust Manager
Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood_access_snapshot.pdf, nb_cross_correlation.csv, forensic_notes.txt
